extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians and comedy writers (performers developing material)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical craft guidance for writing, editing, and performing stand-up jokes—emphasizing specificity, honesty, editing, audience trust, and how to treat bombing as data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: The single most important word in stand-up is 'specifically.' A joke about your mom is generic. A joke about your mom keeping the empty Cool Whip containers because 'you never know when you'll need them' is alive. Specificity is the only way to be universal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concrete, particular details drawn from your life; replace generic premises with vivid specifics that make the bit feel true and relatable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience has a built-in lie detector. If you don't believe what you're saying, they won't either.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid hack premises (airline food, men vs. women) that you don't actually believe; the strongest premises are those the comic genuinely thinks about in daily life (e.g., 'in the shower').

rubrics_metrics.name: Talking vs Material (Editing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Talking is what you do at brunch. Material is what survives compression and stage-testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The difference is editing: a piece of talking becomes material when you've removed every word that doesn't serve the laugh. Continuously compress and stage-test to pare language to what earns the laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bombing (treat as data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bombing is data. It tells you exactly which assumption you got wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a joke bombs, sit with it for 24 hours, then diagnose rather than despair. A bombed joke is recoverable; avoiding stage time prevents the necessary learning. Use bombs to identify false assumptions about premise, structure, or audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience Trust
rubrics_metrics.description: You earn the right to make a hard joke. The first 30 seconds you're on stage, you're auditioning to be trusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with material that establishes you can be funny before asking the audience to follow you to uncomfortable places; prioritize building rapport/trust early in the set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is this premise something I genuinely believe?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working Rubric item: Is this premise something I genuinely believe?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a checklist question to test premise authenticity—if you don't truly believe it, the audience will likely detect the insincerity and the bit will weaken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have I made it as specific as my actual life?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working Rubric item: Have I made it as specific as my actual life?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the premise and details reflect concrete aspects of your lived experience; specificity amplifies truth and universality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the audience trust me to make this joke yet?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working Rubric item: Does the audience trust me to make this joke yet?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess placement and buildup—if trust hasn't been earned (especially within the first ~30 seconds), postpone or rework harder material until rapport is established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have I cut every word that's just talking?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working Rubric item: Have I cut every word that's just talking?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit aggressively to remove filler and conversational excess; only keep words that contribute to the setup, punch, or necessary rhythm—this converts 'talking' into durable 'material.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Am I in service of the laugh, or my ego?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working Rubric item: Am I in service of the laugh, or my ego?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize choices that maximize the laugh rather than showcasing cleverness or self-image; avoid bits that read as ego-driven rather than audience-serving.

rubrics_metrics.name: If this bombs, do I know why?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working Rubric item: If this bombs, do I know why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a diagnosis-ready mindset: when a joke fails, identify which assumption, line, or timing failed. Allow a cooling-off period (24 hours) before troubleshooting and rewriting.
